g.text: What made you want to become a soldier?
What was it like growing up, you and Eleanor?
Yeah. Isn't that how this is supposed to work?
Do you think I know you well enough to jump into that?
Right. Stranded in an alternate dimension.
I'm just trying to get to know you better.
You're less used to "people" than I am.
Going right into my deep personal history isn't the way to do it, mate.
So how am I supposed to do it?
Do I just stop now, or...?
You have to buy a man a few drinks first.
Drinks first. *Then* personal questions. Got it.
Not worth the trouble, never mind. [End.]
Heh. At least you learn quick.
I put him in the tank, the water turned gray a minute later.
If it was, I'd never admit it. Luckily it isn't.
Thought he was going to pop off.
On the first try, too. How'd you know?
Let me put you out of your misery, or we'll be at this all day.
Did this get you what you were looking for?
That's a *place,* not a name, you daftie!
I assume you fixed the water issue.
Sure, if that's all you're willing to share.
Yeah, we'll call that good enough for now.
Black isn't even a real color, anyway. [End.]
I don't know that much about you two, actually.
The bandana you have around your skana.
You just "feel" like a red guy.
Sorry I'm not up to date on my 20th-Century Britannic names!
How was I supposed to know?
Yes, I fixed the damn water.
Couldn't be trusted with anything bigger.
Didn't figure you for the pedantic type.
And I'm not about to start unloading family history to you, so don't try.
Yeah, well. Not like I chose it.
I think I'm going to cry, I'm laughing so hard.
There's a big gap between "what's your favourite colour" and "tell me your family history."
How'd you get that sword, anyway? It never seems to leave your side.
What were your lives like, before all this?
I take after the smart one. ;)
Just wasn't that kind of kid, is all.
There's a big gap between "what's your middle name" and "tell me your family history."
And with that attitude, you won't. [End.]
A long story for another day. After drinks. Anyway.
Careful, or it's going to be what I call you now.
There's a big gap between "what was your first pet" and "tell me your family history."
There's a big gap between "ask me some silly questions" and "tell me your family history."
It's James, by the way. And thanks for the laugh.
Something to work toward, I suppose.
